sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].

The path was cyclical rather than steady: a 20.4% jump in FY2018 to $54.7 billion [F3][D92], a 22.4% collapse in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], then a 22.1% rebound in FY2021 to $51.0 billion [F6][D251].

The FY2020 decline came from lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59], and the FY2021 rebound from higher end-user demand and favorable dealer inventory changes [P50].
FY2023 was the margin peak, with operating margin up 6.0pp to 19.3% [F28][D370], driven by favorable price realization, higher volume and the absence of the 2022 Rail goodwill impairment [P31].
In FY2025 Power & Energy was the growth engine, adding 5.2pp of the 4.3% revenue increase on 11.6% segment growth [D759][D463][D758].
Power Generation sales rose 32.5% to $10.3 billion [S183][D894], while Construction Industries fell 1.6% on $1.136 billion of unfavorable price realization [D765][P8].
North America supplied 3.4pp of FY2025 growth and 54.2% of revenue [D515][D513], with sales up 6.4% on higher equipment sales to end users [D514][P12].
Profit did not keep pace: operating income fell 14.7% against 4.3% revenue growth [D464][D463], an incremental margin of -69.1% [D488].
Per-share decline was milder than net income decline, -14.7% versus -17.7% [D467][D465], as the diluted count fell 3.5% [D483].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 [F30] sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1123][D1122].

The 3.7pp margin decline [D476] came mostly from cost of revenue, a -4.2pp effect [D490], as operating profit fell on $2.148 billion of unfavorable manufacturing costs largely from higher tariffs [P9].
Cost of revenue rose 11.3% against 4.3% revenue growth [D478][D463], lifting its share of revenue to 66.2% from 62.0% [D441][D388].
Net margin fell 3.5pp to 13.1% [F50][D477], a smaller drop than operating margin because other income of $892 million and a 24.0% tax rate cushioned the fall [X110][D449].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion and free cash flow of $8.9 billion [F80][F100] covered net income 1.32x and 1.00x respectively [D450][D451].
Free cash flow margin of 13.2% [D447] is above the 11.9% window median but below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D1129][D1128].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion [F90][D470], lifting capex to 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x D&A [D446][D452], which the filing attributes partly to an increase in capital expenditures [P3].
Machinery operating cash flow still rose on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes, partly offset by inventories and receivables [P4].
Net debt widened to $26.2 billion in FY2025 from $24.9 billion [D456][D403], as total debt grew 14.1% to $36.2 billion while cash rose 44.9% to $10.0 billion [D485][D455][D484][F140].
Net debt is 38.8% of revenue [D457], a heavier net debt load than the 35.6% net debt peer median, ranking at the 43rd percentile of seven peers [D1152][D1151].
Return on average equity of 43.5% ranks at the 100th percentile of six peers against a 23.3% median [D462][D1155][D1156].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow [X140][X150][D459], and the diluted count fell 3.5% [D483].
Net cash has fallen for two straight years into deeper net debt, from -$22.1 billion in FY2023 to -$26.2 billion in FY2025 [D350][D456], as debt rose faster than cash [D485][D484].
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 to $64.8 billion [F9][D410] on lower equipment sales to end users [P22], a one-year dip that reversed in FY2025 [D463].
Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded, differing from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20], so 10-K figures should be used where precision matters.
Segment revenue members overlap and sum to 219% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 [R6], so segment lines must not be added together.
Operating margin: a print below the 14.3% window median [D1123] would confirm the FY2025 cost squeeze, while a return toward the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1122] would reverse it; watch the FY2026 10-K.

Free cash flow margin: holding above the 11.9% median [D1129] would show the capex step-up is digestible, while a drop below the 9.7% FY2018 low [D1127] would signal strain; watch the FY2026 cash flow statement.

Net debt: a further widening beyond the FY2025 $26.2 billion [D456] would extend the two-year trend, while a move back toward the FY2023 $22.1 billion [D350] would reverse it; watch the FY2026 balance sheet.
